newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila firms hold wheat buying await price falls.
newsitem.headline: Manila firms hold wheat buying await price falls.

text.p: Philippine flour millers will probably hold off purchases of wheat this week and wait for current prices to soften, traders said on Monday.
"With these prices, we have to think twice. We still have supplies...so we may just buy on a need basis or if prices soften," said one trader.

Another trader said a flour mill is planning to purchase 35,000 tonnes of wheat, but only if prices dip to lower levels. The trader did not indicate at what price level the flour firm would be likely to enter the market.
The price of the March spring wheat contract in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of its wheat, closed nine U.S. cents lower at US$3.85-1/4 a bushel on Friday.
No wheat transactions were made last week, the traders said. Manila flour mills bought 40,000 tonnes of wheat through a Japanese commodity house in the preceding week.

Of the 40,000 tonnes, 11,000 tonnes of western white wheat were bought for $153-$154 a tonne FOB and 15,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 13.5 percent protein content was purchased at between $178 to $179 a tonne FOB.
The remaining 14,000 tonnes were dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content sold to the millers from $181 to $182 a tonne FOB.

In the rice market, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said this week the Philippines may need to import between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of the staple during the seasonally lean supply period in the third quarter of this year.

The Department of Trade and Industry said the price of hard flour, which is used in making bread, was steady at 290 pesos per 25 kg bag, while the price of soft flour, used in making cakes and pastries, was unchanged at 260 pesos.
Traders said the average retail price of white corn was indicated at 11.55 pesos a kg from 11.93 pesos lastt week and yellow corn at 10.52 pesos a kg from 10.71 pesos.
